subject: Private Offer request and buyer approval gates for Acme Health
messages:
From: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private Offer Request & Approval Path for Acme Health

Vanessa / Redwood team,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the performance numbers look promising for our inference-heavy workflows. Procurement and Legal are starting the vendor intake and we want to move this through the AWS Marketplace private offer route to simplify internal purchasing. Before we open a private offer, can you confirm the following?

- Term options you support (12/24/36 months) and whether unit pricing changes materially by term.
- What discount tiers are available for committed monthly spend vs. annual prepay?
- Any buyer approval thresholds on the AWS side (i.e., will our procurement portal auto-approve <$250k vs. >$250k needs senior buyer signoff)?
- Do you have an example approval matrix we can attach to our internal RFC?

We'll likely loop in our legal (legal@acmehealth.com) on terms and need a first-draft PO/contract to start reviews. Can you also confirm whether Redwood needs a separate Marketplace listing change for Reserved (Dedicated) purchases or if the private offer can reference our existing listing and just override price/term?

Appreciate quick clarity so we can scope our internal timeline.

Thanks,
Marjorie Klein
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Health

Attachment: none

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private Offer Request & Approval Path for Acme Health

Marjorie — thanks for the clear list. Glad the demo resonated. Answers below and I attached a short matrix you can drop into your RFC.

- Term options: 12 / 24 / 36 months supported. Baseline list pricing is the same for 12 vs 24 but we typically offer a 6–12% effective discount for 24 and 10–18% for 36 depending on commit / prepay cadence. See attached "Redwood_PrivateOffer_TermOptions.pdf" for examples.
- Discount tiers: we publish recommended guidance (attached "ApprovalMatrix_Acme.xlsx"). Typical levers: annual prepay, committed monthly throughput, and volume-based escalators. We can do a custom tier for a strategic anchor customer like Acme.
- Buyer approval thresholds (AWS): this is determined by the buyer's AWS Marketplace procurement controls. In our experience with enterprise buyers, private offers >$250k often require a secondary approval by senior procurement / finance. We can include an "Approval Rationale" block in the offer packet to speed that review.
- Marketplace listing change: no listing change required. Private offer will reference your existing Marketplace listing and override price/term. No re-listing needed for Reserved/Dedicated variants; we just map the SKU/offer id.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll draft a PO template and a private-offer cover note for your RFC.
2) Karthik can provide the recommended discount bands and sign-off guidance for commercial approval.
3) Once you confirm target term/commit, we’ll open a private offer in AWS and share the DocuSign/Marketplace link so your procurement can route it.

Attaching: Redwood_PrivateOffer_TermOptions.pdf, ApprovalMatrix_Acme.xlsx

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Cell: (415) 555-0188

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Private Offer Request — Acme Health (need approval gates / pricing guidance)

Karthik / Marcus — forwarding Acme's ask. Key points: they want to understand term/pricing bands, and they flagged internal AWS approval thresholds (likely >$250k needs senior signoff). They asked for an approval matrix to attach to their RFC.

Questions for you:
- Karthik: what discount bands should I propose for 12/24/36 with an initial committed monthly throughput of ~$60k/mo (baseline)? Please include our recommended prepay uplift and the commercial approver notes we can put in the packet.
- Marcus: can you confirm whether a PO/DocuSign we generate will be sufficient for the AWS private offer flow (i.e., will the marketplace record the DocuSign signature and link back properly), and whether there are any AWS-side metadata fields we should populate to reduce buyer review friction?

I've attached a draft PO (RH_PO_Draft_v1.docx) and the approval matrix we gave Acme. I'll iterate once you both chime in. Timeline: Acme wants a packet by Monday 23rd to hit their internal RFC review on Nov 24.

Thanks — Vanessa

> Forwarded message attached: Redwood_PrivateOffer_TermOptions.pdf, ApprovalMatrix_Acme.xlsx, RH_PO_Draft_v1.docx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private Offer Request — Acme Health (need approval gates / pricing guidance)

Thanks Vanessa. Quick answers so you can finalize the packet and send to Marjorie: 

- Recommended bands for $60k/mo baseline:
  * 12mo: list price with 3% recommended sales discount (good for standard procurement cycles)
  * 24mo: 10% effective discount if customer commits to monthly metered commit; 14% if they prepay annually
  * 36mo: 16% effective discount with annual prepay; 12% with monthly commit (we keep flexibility to apply an escalator in year 3)

- Prepay uplift: call out as a separate line item in the offer. We show both the annualized spend and effective unit price so procurement can compare to operating budget flows.

- Approval rationale block (copy to include in packet): 
  "Redwood Inference private offer for Acme Health: 1) Demonstrated performance baseline for inference workloads (latency SLA 99th <= 250ms for standard sizes), 2) Committed monthly throughput and optional annual prepay, 3) Standard Redwood SOC2 Type II compliance; SOC artifacts available on request. This private offer is structured to simplify internal procurement by providing an AWS Marketplace purchase path that maps to existing listing SKUs and will not require additional marketplace relisting. For private offers >$250k, recommend secondary sign-off by VP Procurement or Finance."
- Marcus: on the marketplace/DocuSign side — yes, the DocuSign-signed PO that references the private offer ID is sufficient. Make sure to populate the following AWS-side fields when we open the private offer: buyer_account_id, offer_id (SKU), effective_start/end, negotiated_price_table, and a plain-text approval_rationale field. That reduces ambiguity in buyer portals. Also include a HubSpot deal ID in the offer notes.

Vanessa, draft the packet with these bands and include the approval rationale verbatim. I'll review quickly after.

Karthik
VP, Commercial
